summary: A master's scholarship run by the Asian Development Bank with funding from the Government of Japan, for citizens of ADB's developing member countries. About 135 scholarships a year are available at designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, including Japan, and in Hawaii. You apply to the institution for admission and ask to be considered; there is no separate application to ADB, and ADB makes the final selection.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a national of an ADB borrowing member country that is also eligible for Japanese ODA scholarships, and not hold dual citizenship of a developed country. The programme page lists the eligible citizenships: Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Georgia, India, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Kiribati, Kyrgyz Republic, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nauru, Nepal, Niue, Pakistan, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Turkmenistan, Tuvalu, Uzbekistan, Vanuatu and Viet Nam.

You must be admitted to an approved master's course at a designated institution, and hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent with a superior academic record. You need at least two years of full-time professional work after a university degree, counted at the time of application, and proficiency in spoken and written English. You must be in good health and agree to return home and work there for at least two years after your studies.

You must not be an ADB Executive Director, alternate director, manager, staff member or consultant, or a close relative of one (spouse, parent, step-parent, sibling, step-sibling, child, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew), nor staff of a designated institution. You must not be living or working outside your home country and must not already be enrolled in a graduate degree programme. Past recipients cannot receive a second award.

The FAQ lists how ADB chooses between eligible candidates: the institution's ranking is given priority; women candidates and applicants with lower financial capacity are preferred; applicants who have already studied abroad, or who are seeking a second master's degree, are generally not supported; applicants applying to a designated institution in their own country may not be selected; nationality diversity is considered; and preference goes to candidates with potential to reach senior development roles. The proposed field should link to your background and match ADB Strategy 2030 priorities or Japan's ODA priorities.
age_experience_notes: No more than 35 years old at the time of application; the Government of Japan can waive this only in exceptional cases. At least two years of full-time professional work experience after the university degree, counted at the application date.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays full tuition fees, a monthly subsistence allowance that includes housing, books and instructional materials, medical insurance and travel expenses. Researchers may receive a special grant for thesis preparation, and in special circumstances courses such as computer literacy or preparatory language training can be covered. The award lasts one year and can be extended to a second year if the institution judges performance satisfactory; a master's degree is funded for at most two years. The allowance amount is not stated on the pages I read.
programmes_note: Only the approved fields listed at each designated institution qualify. The programme page groups fields into: science and technology (for example agriculture, biological science, computer science, energy, engineering, environment, forestry, genetics, health); economics, business and management (accounting, business administration, commerce, e-business, entrepreneurship, economics, finance, international cooperation, social sciences); development studies (Asia Pacific studies, development management, development studies); and law and public policy (international business law, international environmental law, policy studies, political science, public administration, public policy). Master's programmes only: the scholarship does not fund undergraduate study, distance learning, short courses, conferences or stand-alone research.
institutions_note: Designated institutions by place, as listed on the ADB institutions page. Hong Kong (China): University of Hong Kong. India: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi. Japan: Hitotsubashi University; Institute of Science Tokyo; International University of Japan; Keio University; Kobe University; Kyoto University; Kyushu University; Nagasaki University; Nagoya University; National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies (GRIPS); Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University; Ritsumeikan University; Saitama University; Tohoku University; UNU-IAS (United Nations University); University of Tokyo; University of Tsukuba. Pakistan: Lahore University of Management Sciences. Philippines: Asian Institute of Management; International Rice Research Institute (registration through the University of the Philippines Los Baños). Singapore: National University of Singapore (NUS Business School, Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, Department of Economics, School of Continuing and Lifelong Education). Thailand: Asian Institute of Technology; Thammasat University. USA: East-West Center, Honolulu. You contact the institution you want, which gives its own application form, intake month and deadline; you may apply to several institutions at once if you say so on each form.

summary.detail: Master's courses only, at designated institutions. The award lasts one year and may be extended to a second year with satisfactory performance. Each institution sets its own intake (months range from January to October) and deadline. The teaching language is not stated; proof of oral and written English is an eligibility requirement.

requirements.text: The institution's own application form for admission, with its required documents, completed and sent to the institution (not to ADB).
The ADB-JSP information sheet (application sheet), sent to the institution together with the admission application. Say on the application that you want to be considered for the scholarship.
Copies of all your academic records.
Your latest income tax return, or a certification of your annual or monthly salary, whichever is available.
A certification of your family income (your parents' income).

application_steps.title: Choose an institution and request its forms
application_steps.detail: Ask the designated institution you prefer for information and application forms, and check its handbook and in-country information sessions before choosing a course. Each institution has its own intake month and deadline.

application_steps.title: Apply to the institution and ask to be considered
application_steps.detail: Tell the institution you are applying for admission and want to be considered for the ADB-JSP scholarship. Send its application form, its required documents, the ADB-JSP information sheet, your academic records, your income tax or salary certificate and your family income certificate. Complete and accurate papers are needed; incomplete applications may not be processed and an award can be cancelled if information proves false.

application_steps.title: Send applications at least six months before the course starts
application_steps.detail: ADB asks for applications at least six months before the start of the intake you want. You may apply to several institutions but must say so on each form. There is no separate application to ADB, and only candidates who are admitted and endorsed by an institution are considered.

application_steps.title: The institution screens and ranks applicants
application_steps.detail: The institution screens and ranks applicants using its own criteria within ADB's eligibility and selection criteria, and may ask candidates for more information. It sends ADB its ranked list with a description of the scoring system.

application_steps.title: ADB recommends awardees; Japan's Executive Director approves
application_steps.detail: ADB reviews the lists and recommends awardees to the Executive Director for Japan, who gives formal approval. ADB then tells the institutions, and the institution informs all applicants. Admission or an endorsement is not a scholarship award: do not change your job until the institution confirms the award.

application_steps.title: Sign the acceptance of the scholarship award
application_steps.detail: Awardees sign an Acceptance of Scholarship Award through the institution, agreeing to return to their home country after their studies. ADB sends a congratulatory letter to the scholar through the university, and the institution starts arrangements for the awardee.

application_steps.title: Study, renew for a second year and return home
application_steps.detail: The award is for one year and can be extended to a second year with satisfactory performance as judged by the institution. After graduating you must return home and work there for at least two years. There is also a two-year restriction on employment with the ADB Group after the programme.
